parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Outline one biochemical treatment for impulse control disorders and non-substance addictive
disorder.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Describe the feeling-state theory (Miller, 2010) as a cognitive cause of impulse control
disorders and non-substance addictive disorder.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
Explain one similarity and one difference between cognitive explanations and behavioural
explanations of impulse control disorders/non-substance addictive disorder.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Describe explanations of schizophrenia and delusional disorder.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Evaluate explanations of schizophrenia and delusional disorder, including a discussion of the
individual versus situational debate. 
Psychology and consumer behaviour

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Explain what is meant by a ‘competitor-focused’ sales technique.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Describe two findings from the study by Kardes et al. (2007) on the disrupt-then-reframe
technique to sell a product.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: Discuss two advantages of field experiments, using examples from the study by Kardes et al.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Describe what psychologists have discovered about intuitive thinking and its imperfections in
consumer decision-making (thinking fast and thinking slow, choice blindness, advertising and
false memory).

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Evaluate what psychologists have discovered about intuitive thinking and its imperfections in
consumer decision-making (thinking fast and thinking slow, choice blindness, advertising and
false memory), including a discussion of reliability. 
Psychology and health

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Explain what is meant by ‘unrealistic optimism’ (Weinstein, 1980) in relation to individual
factors in changing health beliefs.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Describe the procedure used in the study by Janis and Feshbach (1953) on fear arousal.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: Discuss two ethical issues in relation to the study by Janis and Feshbach.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Describe what psychologists have learned about types of non-adherence and reasons why
patients do not adhere to medical advice.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Evaluate what psychologists have learned about types of non-adherence and reasons why
patients do not adhere to medical advice, including a discussion of generalisability. 
Psychology and organisations

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Identify two ‘followership’ types (Kelley, 1988).

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Describe the Leadership Practices Inventory (LPI) devised by Kouzes and Posner (1987).

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: Explain one strength and one weakness of the Leadership Practices Inventory.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Describe what psychologists have discovered about temporal conditions of work
environments.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Evaluate what psychologists have discovered about temporal conditions of work environments,
including a discussion of demand characteristics.
